reports.title: Almonty Industries Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 382% to C$41.9m on tungsten prices but below estimates; Sangdong starts producing; no financial guidance
results: Revenue rose 382% to C$41.9m, driven by a far higher tungsten price, but came in well below the C$70.0m estimate.
Panasqueira in Portugal earned C$26.0m from mining operations, a 62% margin.
Net income of C$50.2m (C$0.17 per diluted share) was mostly non-cash gains on derivatives and warrants; adjusted EBITDA was C$14.6m.
The Sangdong mine in South Korea produced its first concentrate in September, and the first container shipped after quarter end.
Cash reached C$1.15bn after a US$800m convertible bond; about 2.9m shares were bought back in the quarter at an average of US$16.58.

guidance.summary: Almonty gave no revenue or earnings outlook. It plans to ramp up Sangdong Phase I and targets completing the Phase II expansion in 2027, subject to Phase I performance and market conditions.

points: The CEO called Q3 the quarter Sangdong became a commercial operation; the focus is now a safe, steady ramp-up.
More than 90% of Phase I output is contracted to GTP (Plansee Group), on extended terms with about 6.3% better pricing.
Los Santos tailings in Spain and a new Rwanda venture are pitched as quick sources of non-Chinese tungsten.
He pointed to US defence buying rules from 1 Jan 2027 that check where tungsten was mined.
The cash pile is meant to fund growth and the up-to-US$300m buyback.
call.source: No call coverage found; points from CEO comments in the results release

watch: Sangdong ramp-up speed and first full quarter of sales from the mine.
Tungsten (APT) prices, which drive almost all of the revenue growth.
Phase II spending and timing, the switch to US GAAP from January 2027, and buyback pace.
